title: These Goats Climb a 160-Foot Vertical Dam Wall. Just to Lick It

scenes.text: These goats climb a 160 foot vertical dam wall. Just to lick it.
Alpine ibex in northern Italy, hanging off the Cingino Dam like it's a staircase.
The stones are crusted with salt. Grass doesn't have enough, so the ibex go and get it. Fifteen storeys up.
The dam is built from rough stone blocks, and every gap between them is a toehold.
They tiptoe, slide and even gallop across it. Sideways. Over nothing.
One slip is 160 feet down. They still go up. For salt.

description:
Alpine ibex scale the near-vertical 160 foot face of the Cingino Dam in northern Italy to lick salt and minerals off the stones.
The gaps in the dam's rough masonry act as toeholds, and the ibex tiptoe, slide and gallop across the wall; grazing animals cannot get enough salt from plants alone.
Would you climb 160 feet for your favourite snack?
first_comment: Mountain goats in the United States do the same thing on cliffs and even on roadside salt. What is the most ridiculous thing you have seen an animal do for food?
